Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
Comments: MTF survey: urban Tier1+ electricity access 75.2% vs rural 8.7% (gap 66.5 percentage points).
revision_notes: The cited World Bank Beyond Connections report is a genuine 2019 publication (fieldwork 2017) and does support the figures quoted (urban 75.2%, rural 8.7%, gap 66.5pp), so the original code 1 was consistent with that source at the time. However, a more recent and more authoritative primary source is now available: the Zambia Ministry of Energy's 2023 National Energy Access Survey (NEAS) Baseline Report, launched via the Ministry's official website in December 2024, which reports national electricity access of 53.6%, with urban access at 80.3% and rural access at 34.0% — a gap of 46.3 percentage points. This falls within the '2=Gap 41-60pp' band on the metadata scale rather than '1=Gap >60pp'. The gap has narrowed materially, driven mainly by faster rural electrification (rural access roughly quadrupling from 8.7% in 2017 to 34.0% in 2023) alongside urban gains. Score revised from 1 to 2 on this fresher, government-sourced evidence.
revised_comments: Zambia's electrification gap between urban and rural areas has narrowed but remains substantial. The Ministry of Energy's 2023 National Energy Access Survey records electricity access of 80.3% in urban areas compared with 34.0% in rural areas, a gap of roughly 46 percentage points, against a national access rate of 53.6%. Rural access has improved considerably in recent years, though it continues to lag well behind urban areas, with the national grid remaining the dominant electricity source and solar the main alternative.
